title: Same category, three hooks: a 20-minute Ad Library exercise
hook: Line up three ads from your category. Read only the openings.
caption:
Line up three ads from your category. Read only the openings.
What they share tells you where your next ad will blend in.

This is a 20-minute exercise with the public Meta Ad Library. I have shown it on a made-up set of three sunscreen ads, so no real brand is being judged.

Sort each opening into one of three lanes. It opens on a problem, on proof, or on a person. Then count.

One caution on what the count means. The library shows what a brand is running. It does not show what is selling. So a crowded lane is a fact about the feed.

The empty lane is a test worth running on your own ads.

slides.headline: Same category. *Three hooks.*
slides.sub: A 20-minute exercise with the public Ad Library.

slides.headline: What to *collect*
items: Three to five brands — in your category
Their newest video ads — from the public Ad Library
The first three seconds — and nothing after
One row per ad — in a sheet

slides.headline: Every opening picks *one*
items: Proof — shows a result or a test
Person — someone you would listen to

slides.headline: Three *sunscreen* ads
slides.body:
Ad one opens on a white cast in a selfie. Problem.

Ad two opens on a white mark on a dark sleeve. Problem.

Ad three opens on a dermatologist holding the tube. Person.

Nobody opens on proof.

slides.headline: What the count *can tell you*
right: Why an ad is still live

slides.headline: The empty lane is *your test*
slides.body:
In the example, proof is open. So the brief writes itself: open on a UV camera, or a wear test at the beach.

Same product and same message, with a first shot the category is not using.

Then let your own cost per order decide.

slides.headline: Read the openings. *Count the lanes.*
slides.sub: Try it on your category this week.
